stories.title: Dow erases a 1,100-point drop to close +0.33%; S&P 500 −0.25%, Nasdaq −0.62%
stories.body: The S&P 500 closed at 7,182.78 (−0.25%), the Nasdaq at 23,585.80 (−0.62%), the Dow at 50,182.95 (+0.33%) and the Russell 2000 at 2,704.06 (+0.71%) (Yahoo Finance). The Dow erased an intraday decline of more than 1,100 points (Fool); at the lows the Nasdaq was down as much as 4.6% and the S&P 500 3.2% (Beinsure). Reuters said investors sought bargains; Beinsure cited light pre-holiday volume and a Michael Burry post saying his portfolio was "temporarily almost entirely long." SPY closed at $716.70 (−0.29%) and QQQ at $633.93 (−0.65%) (us-market-data).
stories.why: SPY's completed 1-hour closes rose from $699.06 (11:00 AM candle) to $716.71, and QQQ's from $610.41 to $633.81, but none closed above Tuesday's close; with Thursday shut and a 1:00 PM close Friday, the next completed hourly candles come Friday morning.

stories.title: Meta +3.4% bucks the slide; Amazon −3.1% on an AWS traffic note
stories.body: META closed at $609.89 (+3.40%), AMZN at $244.43 (−3.12%), GOOG at $270.98 (−2.02%) and MSFT at $489.93 (−1.25%) (us-market-data). JournalArta tied Meta's gain to a reported $4.5 billion GPU-backed CoreWeave loan for a Meta data center in Georgia and to talks with Amazon about restoring access for its Muse shopping agent. MoneyCheck cited a Bernstein note that activity at usage-based cloud platforms, including AWS, was running about 16% below third-quarter levels in mid-to-late November. The communication services ETF rose 0.89%, consumer discretionary fell 0.20% and technology 0.83% (Market Indicators).
stories.why: META closed near its session high (+3.60%) while AMZN, GOOG and MSFT closed below Tuesday's close despite rebounding from lows of −6.47%, −5.75% and −3.78%; Friday's shortened session leaves few completed 1-hour candles before the weekend.

stories.title: Chips claw back: Micron trims a 13% drop to 4.5%, AMD to 1.8%
stories.body: MU closed at $601.25 (−4.53%) after a session low of −12.97%, AMD at $406.03 (−1.75%, low −10.37%), INTC at $54.47 (−0.60%, low −10.31%) and AVGO at $300.86 (−0.07%, low −7.67%) (us-market-data, Structure One feed). Semiconductor stocks fell on questions about profitability and overinvestment (Yahoo Finance); the chip index was down 1.3% around 3:05 PM ET (Reuters) and closed −0.65% at 8,774.86 (us-market-data). Lam Research fell 5.96% (Reuters), and Ambarella dropped 19.77% after weaker-than-expected guidance (StockTitan, Beinsure).
stories.why: The day's ranges were roughly 7–13% for these four names; a rules-based trader waiting for completed 1-hour closes saw the lows set in the first hours and the recovery confirmed only in afternoon candles.

stories.title: Energy rises with oil; banks end near flat
stories.body: CVX closed at $210.95 (+1.06%), XOM at $158.08 (−0.09%), JPM at $316.74 (−0.11%) and BAC at $48.54 (−0.04%), after BAC fell as much as 3.34% and JPM 2.38% (us-market-data, Structure One feed). The energy sector ETF rose 0.74% and financials 0.71% (Market Indicators); Beinsure said materials, energy and real estate each rose more than 1% in the afternoon. Brent settled 3.5% higher at $94.61 (Rigzone).
stories.why: CVX's rise tracked crude, while XOM closed flat despite the oil move; the banks' near-unchanged closes followed morning drops, so their daily candles show long lower wicks.

stories.title: Nvidia closes −3.9% after an intraday drop of as much as 8%
stories.body: Nvidia closed at $149.30 (−3.91%) after falling as much as 8% during the session, and was $149.73 (+0.29%) after hours (Yahoo Finance). Yahoo Finance said tech sold off on concerns about higher financing costs and profitability. Reuters cited worries about Nvidia after Jensen Huang resigned as CEO earlier this month before the board reinstated him on Monday, along with increased regulatory scrutiny of the AI sector. Huang testifies before Congress next week (Yahoo Finance, citing Bloomberg).
stories.why: NVDA's completed 1-hour closes climbed from $142.14 (12:00 PM candle) to $149.27 but all stayed below Tuesday's $155.38 close; the congressional testimony next week is a scheduled event that can move implied volatility.

stories.title: Gold ETF ends +0.6% after a 3.5% drop; silver ETF recovers from −6.4%
stories.body: GLD closed at $327.45 (+0.61%) and SLV at $37.10 (+0.71%), after session lows of −3.53% and −6.38% (us-market-data, Structure One feed). Gold futures ended at $3,572.40 (+0.29%) (Fool), after spot gold fell as low as $3,446.06 (−3.1%) during the session (TradingNEWS). COMEX silver was down 4.27% at $39.04 in the morning, with Fed Watch hike odds at 97.8% (Upstox).
stories.why: Both metals ETFs closed above Tuesday's close after wide intraday ranges, so a single completed daily candle reversed a morning breakdown; rate-hike pricing remains the backdrop.

stories.title: Brent settles +3.5% at $94.61 as Iran steps up attacks on Hormuz shipping
stories.body: Brent for January settled 3.5% higher at $94.61 and WTI 2% higher at $83.68 (Rigzone). Bloomberg, via Rigzone, said Iran has stepped up attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz and claimed more tankers hit mines since Tuesday, without independent confirmation, and that Saudi forces intercepted four drones fired at Ras Tanura. The Circuitry cited short covering ahead of Thanksgiving and a smaller-than-expected US crude build (1.1 million barrels vs 1.5 million expected); OPEC+ meets Nov. 29. Separately, the USTR proposed Section 301 tariffs on 14 economies, with comments due Jan. 5, 2027 (StockTitan). USO closed at $139.89 (+3.29%) and OXY at $53.95 (+1.07%).
stories.why: USO opened above Tuesday's close and held its gain into the settle; with the OPEC+ meeting on a weekend and Thursday's holiday, news can arrive while US markets are closed.

stories.title: VIX closes up 7.3% at 28.29 despite the late equity rebound
stories.body: The VIX closed at 28.29, up 1.93 points or 7.32% (Yahoo Finance), from 26.36 on Tuesday (Saxo). Early Wednesday, Saxo noted December VIX futures at 24.40 with the term structure in backwardation, the SKEW index elevated at 139.16 and Nasdaq volatility above 36, labeling the regime "high vol bear."
stories.why: Elevated implied volatility raises option premiums and widens expected moves; backwardation means near-dated volatility is priced above later months.

stories.title: 10-year yield eases to 4.86% as 98% December hike odds hold
stories.body: The 10-year Treasury yield eased to 4.86% on Wednesday, down 0.07 percentage point, and the 2-year was 4.65% (Trading Economics). Traders priced a 98% chance of a 25 bp hike in December (Yahoo Finance); Reuters said stronger growth and higher inflation reinforced expectations of a hike next month and again in early 2027. The Fed's Beige Book showed sustained cost pressures, and Freddie Mac's 30-year mortgage rate fell to 7.21% from 7.28% (Yahoo Finance).
stories.why: A hike that is almost fully priced shifts attention to the Dec. 9 decision's guidance; bond markets are closed Thursday and SIFMA recommends a 2:00 PM close Friday.

stories.title: Europe closes lower, DAX −1.23%; KOSPI −6.16% led Asia's chip slide
stories.body: The DAX closed −1.23% at 24,710, the CAC 40 −0.62% at 7,991 and the FTSE 100 −0.32% at 10,434, as AI-valuation worries and the prospect of fresh US tariffs weighed; Infineon fell 6.4% (Trading Economics). In Asia the KOSPI closed −6.16% at 4,697.51 (SK Hynix −7.43%, Samsung −7.18%), the Nikkei −2.78% at 57,011 (SoftBank Group −14.8%), the Shanghai Composite −2.03% at 3,476.47 and the Hang Seng −1.14% at 21,966.01 (Trading Economics).
stories.why: Asia and Europe closed before the US recovery, so Thursday's Asian session is the first to react to Wall Street's late rebound while US markets are shut.

stories.title: Core PCE 3.3% tops forecasts; Q3 GDP revised to 4.3%; claims fall to 189,000
stories.body: October core PCE rose 3.3% y/y vs 3.2% expected (Yahoo Finance), with headline PCE at 3.8% (StockTitan). Q3 GDP was revised up to a 4.3% annual rate from 3.4% (StockTitan), vs a 3.5% forecast (XTB). Initial jobless claims fell 13,000 to 189,000 vs 200,000 expected, and continuing claims were 1.697 million (Rallies). October new home sales came in at a 701,000 annual rate (StockTitan) vs a 650,000 forecast (XTB).
stories.why: Hotter inflation, strong growth and low claims are the data behind the December hike pricing; the releases came out at 8:30 AM ET, before an open that gapped lower (SPY opened at $703.20 vs Tuesday's $718.78 close).

stories.title: Leveraged Nvidia ETF puts jumped 700% Tuesday; skew stays elevated
stories.body: Longbridge reported that the 2x long Nvidia ETF (NVDL) fell 11% to $14.73 on Tuesday as some put options soared 700%; 81,762 NVDL contracts traded, 79% of them calls, and the most active were Nov. 27 calls. Early Wednesday, Saxo noted the SKEW index at 139.16. Eligible options close at 1:15 PM ET on Friday's shortened session (FedRateCalc).
stories.why: Contracts expiring Friday, Nov. 27 trade in a shortened session with a 1:15 PM options close, which compresses the time left for hourly setups before expiration.

stories.title: Ahead: market shut Thursday, 1:00 PM close Friday; OPEC+ meets Nov. 29
stories.body: US stock and bond markets are closed Thursday for Thanksgiving and reopen Friday for a half day (Yahoo Finance); the NYSE closes at 1:00 PM ET, eligible options at 1:15 PM, and SIFMA recommends a 2:00 PM bond close (FedRateCalc). OPEC+ meets Nov. 29 (Saxo, The Circuitry), and January Brent expires Nov. 30 (Saxo). Jensen Huang testifies before Congress next week (Yahoo Finance). The Fed decides Dec. 9 (Saxo), the same day Broadcom reports after the close (Broadcom IR).
stories.why: Friday's session has about three and a half hours, so only a few completed 1-hour closes print before the weekend, when the OPEC+ meeting takes place.

tone.text: Mixed: a chip-led morning rout (Nasdaq −4.6% at the low) was mostly erased; the Dow closed +0.33% and the Russell 2000 +0.71% while the S&P 500 fell 0.25% and the Nasdaq 0.62%, with chips and AI names still lower and the VIX up 7.3% to 28.29.

es.Dow erases a 1,100-point drop to close +: El Dow borra una caída de 1,100 puntos y cierra en +0.33%; S&P 500 −0.25%, Nasdaq −0.62%
es.The S&P 500 closed at 7,182.78 (−0.25%),: El S&P 500 cerró en 7,182.78 (−0.25%), el Nasdaq en 23,585.80 (−0.62%), el Dow en 50,182.95 (+0.33%) y el Russell 2000 en 2,704.06 (+0.71%) (Yahoo Finance). es.SPY's completed 1-hour closes rose from: Los cierres de 1 hora completados de SPY subieron de $699.06 (vela de las 11:00 AM) a $716.71, y los de QQQ de $610.41 a $633.81, pero ninguno cerró por encima del cierre del martes; con el jueves cerrado y el cierre a la 1:00 PM del viernes, las próximas velas horarias completadas llegan el viernes por la mañana.
es.Meta +3.4% bucks the slide; Amazon −3.1%: Meta +3.4% desafía la caída; Amazon −3.1% por una nota sobre el tráfico de AWS
es.META closed at $609.89 (+3.40%), AMZN at: META cerró en $609.89 (+3.40%), AMZN en $244.43 (−3.12%), GOOG en $270.98 (−2.02%) y MSFT en $489.93 (−1.25%) (us-market-data). JournalArta vinculó el avance de Meta a un préstamo reportado de $4,500 millones respaldado por GPU para CoreWeave, destinado a un centro de datos de Meta en Georgia, y a conversaciones con Amazon para restablecer el acceso de su agente de compras Muse. MoneyCheck citó una nota de Bernstein según la cual la actividad en plataformas de nube por uso, incluida AWS, iba cerca de 16% por debajo de los niveles del tercer trimestre a mediados y finales de noviembre. El ETF de servicios de comunicación subió 0.89%, consumo discrecional bajó 0.20% y tecnología 0.83% (Market Indicators).
es.META closed near its session high (+3.60: META cerró cerca de su máximo de sesión (+3.60%), mientras AMZN, GOOG y MSFT cerraron por debajo del cierre del martes pese a rebotar desde mínimos de −6.47%, −5.75% y −3.78%; la sesión corta del viernes deja pocas velas de 1 hora completadas antes del fin de semana.

Las acciones de semiconductores cayeron por dudas sobre la rentabilidad y la sobreinversión (Yahoo Finance); el índice de chips bajaba 1.3% cerca de las 3:05 PM ET (Reuters) y cerró en −0.65% en 8,774.86 (us-market-data). Lam Research cayó 5.96% (Reuters) y Ambarella se desplomó 19.77% tras una guía más débil de lo esperado (StockTitan, Beinsure).
es.The day's ranges were roughly 7–13% for: Los rangos del día fueron de aproximadamente 7–13% para estos cuatro nombres; un trader basado en reglas que espera cierres de 1 hora completados vio los mínimos en las primeras horas y la recuperación confirmada solo en las velas de la tarde.

es.Nvidia closes −3.9% after an intraday dr: Nvidia cierra en −3.9% tras una caída intradía de hasta 8%
es.Nvidia closed at $149.30 (−3.91%) after: Nvidia cerró en $149.30 (−3.91%) tras caer hasta 8% durante la sesión y marcaba $149.73 (+0.29%) fuera de horario (Yahoo Finance). Yahoo Finance dijo que la tecnología se vendió por preocupaciones sobre mayores costos de financiamiento y la rentabilidad. Huang testifica ante el Congreso la próxima semana (Yahoo Finance, citando a Bloomberg).

es.Both metals ETFs closed above Tuesday's: Ambos ETF de metales cerraron por encima del cierre del martes tras amplios rangos intradía, por lo que una sola vela diaria completada revirtió una ruptura matutina; la expectativa de alza de tasas sigue de fondo.
es.Brent settles +3.5% at $94.61 as Iran st: El Brent cierra +3.5% en $94.61 mientras Irán intensifica los ataques a buques en Ormuz
es.Brent for January settled 3.5% higher at: El Brent de enero cerró 3.5% más alto en $94.61 y el WTI 2% más alto en $83.68 (Rigzone). Bloomberg, vía Rigzone, dijo que Irán intensificó los ataques a buques en el estrecho de Ormuz y afirmó que más petroleros chocaron con minas desde el martes, sin confirmación independiente, y que fuerzas saudíes interceptaron cuatro drones lanzados contra Ras Tanura. The Circuitry citó cobertura de cortos antes de Acción de Gracias y un aumento de inventarios de crudo menor al esperado (1.1 millones de barriles vs 1.5 millones esperados); la OPEP+ se reúne el 29 de nov. Por separado, la USTR propuso aranceles de la Sección 301 a 14 economías, con comentarios hasta el 5 de enero de 2027 (StockTitan). USO cerró en $139.89 (+3.29%) y OXY en $53.95 (+1.07%).
es.USO opened above Tuesday's close and hel: USO abrió por encima del cierre del martes y mantuvo su avance hasta la liquidación; con la reunión de la OPEP+ en fin de semana y el feriado del jueves, las noticias pueden llegar con los mercados de EE. UU. cerrados.
es.VIX closes up 7.3% at 28.29 despite the: El VIX cierra con alza de 7.3% en 28.29 pese al rebote tardío de las acciones
es.The VIX closed at 28.29, up 1.93 points: El VIX cerró en 28.29, con alza de 1.93 puntos o 7.32% (Yahoo Finance), desde 26.36 el martes (Saxo). A primera hora del miércoles, Saxo señaló los futuros del VIX de diciembre en 24.40 con la estructura temporal en backwardation, el índice SKEW elevado en 139.16 y la volatilidad del Nasdaq por encima de 36, y calificó el régimen como "bajista de alta volatilidad".
es.Elevated implied volatility raises optio: Una volatilidad implícita elevada encarece las primas de las opciones y amplía los movimientos esperados; el backwardation significa que la volatilidad de corto plazo se cotiza por encima de los meses posteriores.
es.10-year yield eases to 4.86% as 98% Dece: El rendimiento a 10 años baja a 4.86% mientras se mantienen probabilidades de 98% de alza en diciembre
es.The 10-year Treasury yield eased to 4.86: El rendimiento del Tesoro a 10 años bajó a 4.86% el miércoles, 0.07 puntos porcentuales menos, y el de 2 años quedó en 4.65% (Trading Economics). Los operadores descontaron una probabilidad de 98% de un alza de 25 pb en diciembre (Yahoo Finance); Reuters dijo que un mayor crecimiento y una inflación más alta reforzaron las expectativas de un alza el próximo mes y otra a inicios de 2027. El Libro Beige de la Fed mostró presiones de costos sostenidas, y la tasa hipotecaria a 30 años de Freddie Mac bajó a 7.21% desde 7.28% (Yahoo Finance).
es.A hike that is almost fully priced shift: Un alza casi totalmente descontada desplaza la atención a la guía de la decisión del 9 de dic.; el mercado de bonos cierra el jueves y SIFMA recomienda un cierre a las 2:00 PM el viernes.

es.Core PCE 3.3% tops forecasts; Q3 GDP rev: El PCE subyacente de 3.3% supera lo previsto; el PIB del 3T se revisa a 4.3%; las solicitudes bajan a 189,000
es.October core PCE rose 3.3% y/y vs 3.2% e: El PCE subyacente de octubre subió 3.3% anual vs 3.2% esperado (Yahoo Finance), con el PCE general en 3.8% (StockTitan). El PIB del 3T se revisó al alza a una tasa anual de 4.3% desde 3.4% (StockTitan), vs un pronóstico de 3.5% (XTB). Las solicitudes iniciales de desempleo bajaron 13,000 a 189,000 vs 200,000 esperadas, y las continuas fueron 1.697 millones (Rallies). Las ventas de casas nuevas de octubre llegaron a una tasa anual de 701,000 (StockTitan) vs un pronóstico de 650,000 (XTB).
es.Hotter inflation, strong growth and low: Una inflación más caliente, un crecimiento fuerte y pocas solicitudes de desempleo son los datos detrás de la expectativa de alza de diciembre; las cifras salieron a las 8:30 AM ET, antes de una apertura con gap bajista (SPY abrió en $703.20 vs el cierre del martes de $718.78).

es.Contracts expiring Friday, Nov. 27 trade: Los contratos que vencen el viernes 27 de nov. operan en una sesión corta con cierre de opciones a la 1:15 PM, lo que reduce el tiempo disponible para configuraciones horarias antes del vencimiento.
